user_history.review_text: I lived in a lovely 1910 home that still had all the radiators and boiler working perfectly and loved that type of heating.  I have heard it isn't as "efficient" as a furnace that blows heated air through ductwork, but that's not the only consideration.  Number one, is the stuff that circulates in that blown air - so many of us have sensitivities (or allergies) to dust, mold and spores which can all be found in ductwork in houses.  Radiant heating with radiators doesn't blow anything - it simply heats the material inside the metal fins of the radiator and that heat radiates throughout the room.  Nothing moving in the air so nothing getting into the nose or nasal cavities and getting inflamed/irritated.  Second, completely quiet - that was something I absolutely loved about radiators - I do understand that inefficient boilers can make knocking sounds in the pipes, but I never had that issue.  I mention these two pluses because they also apply to this space heater - it is, in effect, a portable radiator.  Quiet and it warms the space around it by just radiating that heat outwards.  I don't make much money so having this to maintain warmth just where I am and keeping my house cooler will save me in heating bills this winter.  I mean, why do I need to heat the entire room to an even temperature if I can roll this radiator around to where I am be it sitting in the living room, making dinner in the kitchen or snuggled under the covers in my bedroom.  This radiator is small enough and with the casters, portable enough to follow me around and keep me comfortable in a house with the thermostat set between 45 and 50 degrees during winter.
